Prepare onion-tomato masala with spices.
Add water to make gravy.
Add eggs and simmer for 5-8 minutes.
Heat oil.
Sauté onion and green chilli.
Add ginger and tomato.
Add turmeric and chilli powder.
Beat eggs and pour into the pan.
Stir continuously until softly scrambled.
Finish with coriander.
Brown onion.
Add ginger-garlic paste.
Add minced meat and fry until moisture evaporates.
Add tomato and spices.
Add peas and water.
Cook covered until keema is completely cooked.
Finish with garam masala.
Mix all ingredients thoroughly.
Refrigerate for 30-60 minutes.
Shape mixture around skewers.
Grill or roast while turning regularly.
Brush with oil or butter.
Cook until the centre is fully done.
Mix and knead the mince thoroughly.
Chill the mixture.
Shape around skewers.
Grill over medium-high heat while turning frequently.
Cook until completely done and lightly charred.
Marinate chicken with lemon and salt.
Mix hung curd, cream, cheese, ginger-garlic, chilli, white pepper and cardamom.
Coat chicken and refrigerate for 3-4 hours.
Thread onto skewers.
Grill until lightly browned and cooked through.
Brush with butter or cream while grilling.
Combine minced chicken with all ingredients.
Chill the mixture.
Shape around skewers.
Grill over medium-high heat.
Turn and baste with butter or oil.
Cook until completely done while keeping the kebab moist.
Make cuts in the fish.
Marinate with lemon, salt and turmeric.
Apply yogurt-spice marinade.
Refrigerate for 1-2 hours.
Grill at high heat.
Turn and baste with oil.
Cook until fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Marinate chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chilli, turmeric and lemon.
Heat oil and fry whole spices.
Add marinated chicken.
Add fried onion, green chilli, mint and coriander.
Add nut paste and a little water.
Cover and cook until chicken is tender.
Finish with garam masala and fresh coriander.
Marinate mutton with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chilli, turmeric, lemon and optional raw papaya paste.
Rest for 1-2 hours.
Fry whole spices in oil.
Add marinated mutton and brown well.
Add fried onions, green chillies, mint and coriander.
Add water and cook slowly or pressure-cook until tender.
Reduce the gravy.
Finish with garam masala and coriander.
Preheat the oven to 240°C and place a pizza stone or tray inside to heat.
Stretch the dough into a thin round and place it on a lightly floured surface or pizza peel.
Spread passata over the dough, leaving a small border, then add mozzarella and a little salt.
Bake for 8–12 minutes until the crust is browned and the cheese is bubbling.
Top with fresh basil and olive oil, then serve hot.
Preheat the oven to 240°C with a pizza tray or stone inside.
Stretch the dough into a round and spread the pizza sauce evenly.
Add mozzarella, then arrange pepperoni slices over the cheese.
Sprinkle with oregano and bake for 8–12 minutes until the crust is golden and cheese is melted.
Drizzle lightly with olive oil and serve hot.
Preheat the oven to 240°C.
Stretch the pizza dough into a round and brush lightly with olive oil.
Distribute mozzarella, parmesan, blue cheese and provolone evenly over the dough.
Bake for 8–12 minutes until the crust is crisp and the cheeses are melted and lightly browned.
Rest for 2 minutes, slice and serve.

ingredients: Salt and black pepper – to taste
steps: Cook fettuccine in salted boiling water until al dente; reserve about 1/2 cup pasta water.
Melt butter in a pan and gently sauté garlic.
Add cream and simmer for 2–3 minutes.
Add Parmesan and stir until smooth; loosen with reserved pasta water if needed.
Toss in the pasta, season with salt and pepper, and serve immediately.

ingredients: Pecorino Romano or Parmesan – 75 g, grated
steps: Cook spaghetti in salted water until al dente and reserve some pasta water.
Cook pancetta or guanciale in a dry pan until crisp.
Whisk egg, yolks, cheese and black pepper in a bowl.
Remove the pasta from heat and toss with the meat; add the egg mixture while tossing quickly, using pasta water to make a creamy sauce.
Serve immediately with extra cheese and black pepper.
Heat olive oil and sauté onion, carrot, celery and garlic until softened.
Add ground beef and cook until browned.
Stir in tomato paste and crushed tomatoes with the herbs.
Simmer gently for 20–30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cook spaghetti until al dente, drain and serve with the Bolognese sauce.
Prepare a meat sauce by sautéing onion and garlic, browning beef and simmering it with tomatoes.
Mix ricotta with a little salt and pepper.
Layer meat sauce, lasagna sheets, ricotta and mozzarella in a baking dish, repeating the layers.
Finish with meat sauce, mozzarella and Parmesan.
Bake at 190°C for about 35–45 minutes, rest for 10–15 minutes and serve.

ingredients: Vegetable or chicken stock – 4 cups, warm
steps: Sauté mushrooms in olive oil until browned; set aside.
Cook onion and garlic in the pan, then add Arborio rice and toast for 1–2 minutes.
Add wine if using and let it absorb.
Add warm stock one ladle at a time, stirring and allowing each addition to absorb before adding more.
Stir in mushrooms, butter and Parmesan; season and serve creamy.

ingredients: Salt and black pepper – to taste
steps: Mix diced tomatoes with basil, olive oil, salt, pepper and balsamic vinegar if using.
Slice the bread and toast or grill until crisp.
Rub the warm bread lightly with a cut garlic clove.
Spoon the tomato mixture over the toasted bread.
Serve immediately.

ingredients: Butter or olive oil – for serving
steps: Boil or bake potatoes until tender, then peel and mash while warm.
Mix with egg, salt and enough flour to form a soft dough; avoid overworking.
Roll into ropes and cut into small pieces, shaping with a fork if desired.
Boil gnocchi in salted water until they float, then cook for another 1–2 minutes.
Drain and toss with butter, olive oil or your preferred sauce.
Cook macaroni until just al dente and drain.
Melt butter, whisk in flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in milk and cook until the sauce thickens.
Remove from heat and stir in cheeses, mustard, salt and pepper.
Mix with macaroni and serve, or bake at 190°C for 15–20 minutes for a browned top.
Pound chicken to even thickness and season with salt and pepper.
Coat each piece in flour, beaten egg, then breadcrumbs mixed with Parmesan.
Pan-fry until golden and nearly cooked through.
Place chicken in a baking dish, top with tomato sauce and mozzarella.
Bake at 200°C for about 15–20 minutes until cooked through and cheese is melted.

ingredients: Salt and black pepper – to taste
steps: Cook fettuccine until al dente and reserve some pasta water.
Season and cook chicken in butter until golden and fully cooked; remove from the pan.
Sauté garlic, add cream and simmer briefly.
Stir in Parmesan and enough pasta water to make a smooth sauce.
Return chicken and pasta to the pan, toss well and garnish with parsley.

ingredients: Beef steak – 2 steaks, about 200–250 g each
Salt and black pepper – to taste
steps: Bring steaks close to room temperature and pat them dry; season generously.
Heat a heavy skillet until very hot and add oil.
Sear steaks for about 2–4 minutes per side depending on thickness and desired doneness.
Add butter, garlic and herbs and baste the steaks for about 1 minute.
Rest for 5–10 minutes before slicing and serving.

ingredients: Salt and black pepper – to taste
Burger sauce or mayonnaise – as needed
steps: Divide beef into four portions and shape gently into patties.
Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Cook patties on a hot grill or skillet until browned and cooked to the desired doneness; add cheese near the end.
Toast the buns lightly and spread with sauce.
Assemble with lettuce, tomato, onion and the beef patty, then serve.
Flatten chicken fillets evenly and season with paprika, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Dip chicken in beaten egg and coat with breadcrumbs.
Pan-fry or bake until golden and the chicken reaches 74°C internally.
Toast buns and spread with mayonnaise.
Assemble with lettuce, tomato and cooked chicken, then serve.

ingredients: Cold sparkling water or beer – 1 1/4 cups
steps: Cut potatoes into chips, rinse and dry thoroughly.
Mix flour and cornstarch with cold sparkling water to make a smooth batter.
Heat oil to about 175°C and fry the chips until pale and partly cooked; drain.
Dip fish in batter and fry until crisp and cooked through.
Finish frying the chips until golden, season with salt and serve with the fish.
Cut chicken into bite-sized pieces and season.
Coat each piece in flour, beaten egg and seasoned breadcrumbs.
For frying, heat oil to about 175°C; for baking, place on a lined tray and brush lightly with oil.
Fry until golden and cooked through, or bake at 200°C for about 15–20 minutes, turning once.
Serve hot with a dipping sauce.

ingredients: Hot sauce or barbecue sauce – 1/2 cup
steps: Pat the wings dry and toss with oil, paprika, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Arrange in a single layer on a lined baking tray.
Bake at 220°C for about 35–45 minutes, turning once, until crisp and cooked through.
Toss the hot wings with hot sauce or barbecue sauce.
Serve immediately.

ingredients: Salt and black pepper – to taste
steps: Mix oil, lemon juice, garlic, paprika, salt and pepper and coat the chicken.
Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or refrigerate for several hours.
Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Grill chicken until browned and the center reaches 74°C, turning as needed.
Rest for 5 minutes before slicing and serving.
Wash, dry and chop the romaine lettuce.
Whisk mayonnaise, lemon juice, garlic, mustard and olive oil into a dressing.
Toss lettuce with the dressing until lightly coated.
Add croutons and Parmesan and toss again.
Season with black pepper and serve immediately.
Chop cucumber, tomatoes, onion and bell pepper.
Combine the vegetables with olives in a large bowl.
Whisk olive oil, vinegar and oregano together.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss gently.
Top with feta and serve.

ingredients: Cooked seasoned meat or beans – 400 g
steps: Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet.
Prepare the chosen filling with seasoning until hot and cooked.
Fill each tortilla with the meat or beans.
Add lettuce, tomato, cheese, salsa and sour cream.
Fold and serve immediately.

ingredients: Chicken breast or thigh – 400 g, diced
steps: Toss chicken with lime juice, chili powder, cumin, salt and pepper.
Cook chicken in a hot skillet until browned and cooked through.
Add onion and bell pepper and sauté until slightly tender.
Warm the tortillas.
Fill tortillas with chicken and vegetables and top with lettuce and salsa.
Brown the ground beef with onion in a skillet.
Add chili powder, cumin, salt and pepper and cook until the beef is fully cooked.
Warm the taco shells or tortillas.
Fill with seasoned beef and add lettuce, tomato and cheese.
Serve with salsa or sour cream if desired.
Sauté onion and bell pepper until slightly softened and mix with chicken.
Place a tortilla in a lightly oiled skillet and add cheese, chicken mixture and more cheese.
Top with another tortilla and cook until the underside is golden.
Flip carefully and cook until the second side is golden and the cheese melts.
Cut into wedges and serve with salsa.
Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Spread tortilla chips on a baking tray and scatter beans and cheese over them.
Bake for 5–8 minutes until the cheese melts.
Top with jalapeños and diced tomato.
Serve immediately with sour cream, salsa and guacamole.

ingredients: Cooked shredded chicken or beef – 400 g
steps: Sauté onion and combine with the cooked filling.
Dip tortillas briefly in warm enchilada sauce to soften.
Fill and roll each tortilla, then place seam-side down in a baking dish.
Cover with remaining sauce and cheese.
Bake at 190°C for 20–25 minutes until bubbling.
Warm the tortillas so they are flexible.
Place rice, beans, meat, cheese, salsa, sour cream and lettuce in the center.
Fold the sides inward and roll tightly from the bottom.
Toast the wrapped burrito seam-side down in a skillet if desired.
Slice and serve warm.
Toss the meat with lime juice, chili powder, cumin, salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a skillet and cook the meat until browned and cooked through.
Add peppers and onion and stir-fry until tender-crisp.
Warm the tortillas.
Serve the sizzling filling in tortillas with salsa or sour cream.
Cut avocados, remove the pits and scoop the flesh into a bowl.
Mash the avocado with a fork, leaving some texture.
Stir in tomato, onion, cilantro and jalapeño if using.
Add lime juice and salt and mix gently.
Serve immediately with tortilla chips or as a topping.
Bring water, butter, sugar and salt to a boil.
Add flour and stir vigorously until a smooth dough forms; cool slightly and mix in the egg if using.
Pipe strips of dough into oil heated to about 175°C.
Fry until golden and crisp, then drain on paper towels.
Roll in cinnamon sugar and serve.
Melt butter with olive oil and cook onions over low-medium heat until deeply caramelized, about 30–40 minutes.
Add thyme, salt and pepper.
Pour in beef stock and simmer for 15–20 minutes.
Ladle soup into ovenproof bowls and top with toasted baguette and Gruyère.
Broil until the cheese is melted and browned, then serve carefully.
Heat olive oil and sauté onion and garlic.
Add eggplant and cook until it begins to soften.
Add zucchini and bell pepper and cook for several minutes.
Add tomatoes, herbs, salt and pepper and simmer gently until all vegetables are tender.
Adjust seasoning and serve warm or at room temperature.
Make a béchamel by melting butter, whisking in flour, then gradually adding milk until thick; season with nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Spread béchamel on bread slices and layer with ham and cheese.
Close the sandwiches and spread more béchamel and cheese on top.
Bake at 200°C until the sandwiches are hot and the cheese is bubbling and browned.
Serve immediately.

ingredients: Salt, pepper and nutmeg – to taste
steps: Preheat oven to 190°C and blind-bake the crust for about 10 minutes.
Cook bacon until lightly crisp; drain excess fat.
Whisk eggs, cream, milk, seasoning and nutmeg.
Scatter bacon and cheese in the crust and pour in the egg mixture.
Bake for about 30–40 minutes until the center is set. Cool slightly before slicing.
Brown the bacon and chicken pieces in a heavy pot; remove and set aside.
Sauté onion, carrots, garlic and mushrooms.
Return chicken and bacon, add tomato paste and pour in red wine and stock.
Add thyme and simmer covered until the chicken is tender, about 45–60 minutes.
Adjust seasoning and serve with bread, potatoes or noodles.
Brown the bacon and beef in batches in a heavy pot.
Sauté onion, carrots and garlic, then stir in tomato paste.
Return beef and add red wine and beef stock with thyme.
Cover and simmer gently for about 2–3 hours until the beef is tender.
Add mushrooms near the end, adjust seasoning and serve.
Heat olive oil in a wide paella pan and brown chicken and chorizo if using.
Add pepper and tomatoes and cook until softened.
Stir in paprika and rice, then add saffron-infused stock.
Arrange shrimp and peas over the rice and cook without stirring until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve with lemon wedges.
Heat olive oil and gently cook potatoes and onion until tender, without browning heavily.
Drain most of the oil and let the potato mixture cool slightly.
Beat eggs with salt and mix with the potatoes and onion.
Pour into a nonstick pan and cook over medium-low heat until mostly set.
Flip carefully and cook the other side until set, then slice and serve.
Cut potatoes into bite-sized cubes and rinse and dry them.
Fry or roast potatoes until crisp and golden.
For the bravas sauce, sauté garlic, add passata, paprika and vinegar, and simmer until thick.
Season the sauce and spoon it over the hot potatoes.
Serve with aioli or mayonnaise.
Slice eggplant, salt lightly and roast or pan-cook until tender.
Sauté onion and garlic, brown the meat and simmer with tomatoes and cinnamon.
Layer eggplant and meat sauce in a baking dish.
Spread béchamel over the top and sprinkle with Parmesan.
Bake at 180°C for 40–45 minutes until browned; rest before slicing.
Mix oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper and marinate the meat for at least 30 minutes.
Thread the meat onto skewers.
Grill over medium-high heat until browned and cooked through, turning regularly.
Warm the pita breads.
Serve skewers with pita, tzatziki and salad.
Drain soaked chickpeas thoroughly and blend with onion, garlic, herbs and spices until finely ground but not smooth.
Mix in flour and shape into small balls or patties.
Fry in about 175°C oil until crisp and golden, or bake until browned.
Warm the flatbreads and spread with tahini sauce.
Add falafel and salad, wrap tightly and serve.
Blend chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic and salt until smooth.
Add cold water gradually until the hummus reaches a creamy consistency.
Taste and adjust lemon juice and salt.
Spread hummus onto a plate and make a shallow swirl with a spoon.
Drizzle with olive oil and garnish with paprika and parsley; serve with pita and vegetables.
Heat olive oil and sauté onion and bell pepper until softened.
Add garlic, paprika and cumin and cook briefly.
Add tomatoes and simmer for 10–15 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Make wells in the sauce and crack the eggs into them; cover and cook until the whites are set and yolks are at the desired doneness.
Garnish with herbs and serve with bread.

ingredients: Thai eggplant or mixed vegetables – 2 cups
steps: Heat oil and fry the green curry paste for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Add a little coconut milk and cook the paste briefly.
Add chicken and cook until nearly done.
Add remaining coconut milk, vegetables, fish sauce and sugar; simmer until the chicken and vegetables are cooked.
Stir in Thai basil and serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.
Soft-boil the eggs for about 6–7 minutes, cool, peel and halve.
Heat broth with garlic, ginger, soy sauce and miso until steaming.
Cook ramen noodles separately according to the package directions and drain.
Place noodles in bowls and pour over the hot broth.
Top with egg, spring onion and vegetables and serve immediately.
Season beef with soy sauce and a little sesame oil, then stir-fry until cooked.
Cook spinach, carrots, mushrooms and bean sprouts separately until just tender.
Divide hot rice among bowls and arrange the vegetables and beef over it.
Fry eggs and place one on each bowl.
Serve with gochujang and sesame oil; mix everything together before eating.

ingredients: Fresh herbs and lime – for serving
steps: Blanch the beef bones, rinse them, then simmer with onion and ginger in fresh water for a clear broth.
Toast star anise and cinnamon briefly and add them to the broth; simmer for several hours, skimming as needed.
Strain the broth and season with fish sauce and sugar.
Cook rice noodles according to the package directions and divide among bowls.
Top with thin beef slices, pour over very hot broth, and serve with bean sprouts, herbs and lime.
Make a soft dough by mixing milk powder, flour, baking soda and ghee, adding milk little by little.
Rest the dough for 5–10 minutes, then form small smooth balls without cracks.
Heat oil or ghee on low-medium heat and fry the balls slowly until evenly golden brown.
Boil sugar, water and cardamom for about 5–7 minutes to make a light syrup; add rose water if desired.
Soak the warm fried jamuns in the warm syrup for at least 1–2 hours before serving.

ingredients: 1–2 tbsp lemon juice, diluted with water
steps: Boil half the milk and curdle it gradually with diluted lemon juice. Strain the chhena, rinse and hang it to drain.
Knead the chhena until smooth, divide it into portions and flatten into small discs.
Boil sugar and water, add the discs and cook covered for about 12–15 minutes until puffed.
Reduce the remaining milk over medium heat until creamy and slightly thick, then add sugar, cardamom, saffron and nuts.
Gently squeeze the cooked discs and soak them in the prepared rabri. Chill before serving.

ingredients: 1/4 tsp turmeric or a small amount of orange food color (optional)
steps: Mix flour, cornflour and yogurt with water into a thick, smooth batter. Rest or ferment it for 8–12 hours for traditional flavor.
Prepare a one-string sugar syrup with sugar, water and cardamom; add lemon juice to prevent crystallization.
Transfer batter to a squeeze bottle or piping bag.
Pipe spirals into medium-hot oil and fry until crisp and golden.
Immediately dip the jalebis in warm syrup for about 20–30 seconds, then serve.
Rinse and soak rice for 15–20 minutes, then drain.
Bring milk to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add rice and cook on low heat, stirring frequently.
Cook until the rice is soft and the milk thickens.
Add sugar, cardamom, saffron, nuts and raisins; simmer for another 5–8 minutes.
Serve warm or chilled.
Wash, peel and grate the carrots.
Cook carrots with milk in a heavy pan until the milk is mostly absorbed and the carrots are tender.
Add sugar and continue cooking until the mixture thickens.
Add ghee, cardamom, nuts and raisins and cook for another 5–8 minutes.
Serve warm or chilled.
Boil milk and curdle it with diluted lemon juice. Strain and rinse the chhena well.
Hang the chhena for about 30 minutes, then knead until smooth and slightly soft.
Shape into small crack-free balls.
Boil sugar and water in a wide pan. Add the balls, cover and cook for about 15–18 minutes.
Cool slightly and serve soaked in the syrup.
Bring milk to a boil in a heavy pan and simmer, stirring often, until reduced by roughly one-third to one-half.
Add sugar, saffron and cardamom and simmer until creamy.
Stir in chopped nuts and cool the mixture completely.
Pour into kulfi molds or small containers and freeze for at least 6 hours.
Unmold briefly under warm water and serve.

ingredients: 1 cup hot water or hot coffee
steps: Preheat the oven to 175°C and grease a cake pan.
Whisk flour, cocoa, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
Add eggs, milk, oil and vanilla and mix until combined.
Stir in hot water or coffee carefully; the batter will be thin.
Bake for about 30–35 minutes, or until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool before serving or frosting.
Preheat oven to 175°C and grease a cake pan.
Cream butter and sugar until light. Beat in eggs one at a time, then add vanilla.
Mix flour, baking powder and salt separately.
Add dry ingredients to the butter mixture alternately with milk, mixing just until combined.
Bake for about 30–35 minutes. Cool before slicing.
Preheat oven to 175°C and prepare two cake pans.
Whisk flour, sugar, baking soda, cocoa and salt.
Mix buttermilk, oil, eggs, vanilla, coloring and vinegar.
Combine wet and dry ingredients without overmixing.
Divide into pans and bake about 25–30 minutes. Cool completely before frosting with cream cheese frosting.

ingredients: 1 chocolate sponge cake, baked and cooled
steps: Slice the cooled chocolate cake horizontally into layers.
Whip cream with powdered sugar and vanilla until stiff peaks form.
Brush each cake layer lightly with cherry syrup, then spread cream and add cherries.
Stack the layers and cover the cake with whipped cream.
Decorate with chocolate shavings and cherries; chill before serving.
Crush biscuits and mix with melted butter. Press into the base of a lined springform pan.
Beat cream cheese and sugar until smooth.
Beat in eggs one at a time, then mix in vanilla and sour cream.
Pour over the crust and bake at 160°C for about 45–55 minutes until the center is just set.
Cool gradually, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours before slicing.
Preheat oven to 160°C. Make a biscuit-and-butter crust and press firmly into a springform pan.
Beat cream cheese and sugar until smooth, avoiding excessive aeration.
Add eggs one at a time, followed by vanilla, sour cream and lemon juice.
Pour into the crust and bake until the edges are set and the center has a slight wobble, about 55–70 minutes.
Cool completely and refrigerate for several hours before serving.
Preheat oven to 175°C and line a square baking pan.
Melt butter and whisk with sugar. Add eggs and vanilla.
Fold in flour, cocoa and salt until just combined.
Fold in chocolate chips if using.
Bake about 20–25 minutes. Cool before cutting.
Preheat oven to 175°C and line a square pan.
Melt butter and chocolate together. Whisk in sugar, eggs and vanilla.
Fold in flour, cocoa and salt just until combined.
Spread into the pan and bake for about 20–25 minutes; do not overbake.
Cool fully for a dense, fudgy texture before cutting.
Melt chocolate gently and let it cool slightly.
Whisk egg yolks into the chocolate mixture.
Whip cream with vanilla until soft peaks form.
Whip egg whites with sugar until glossy peaks form.
Fold whipped cream and then egg whites gently into the chocolate. Chill for at least 2 hours.
Sprinkle gelatin over cold water and let it bloom.
Warm milk and dissolve the bloomed gelatin in it; cool slightly.
Whip cream with sugar and vanilla to soft peaks.
Fold the cooled milk mixture gently into the cream.
Divide into serving glasses and refrigerate until set.

ingredients: 1/2 cup mango or other seasonal fruit
steps: Mix custard powder with a little cold milk to make a smooth slurry.
Heat remaining milk with sugar. Add the slurry and cook while stirring until thick.
Cool the custard completely.
Fold in chopped fruits just before serving.
Chill for at least 1 hour.

ingredients: 1 cup pastry cream or thick custard
steps: Mix flour, sugar and cold butter until crumbly. Add egg yolk and enough cold water to form dough.
Chill the dough for 30 minutes, then roll and line a tart pan.
Prick the base and bake at 180°C for about 18–22 minutes until golden. Cool.
Fill with pastry cream and arrange fresh fruit on top.
Chill until ready to serve.
Make a pie dough with flour, salt, sugar and cold butter, adding cold water as needed. Chill.
Toss sliced apples with sugar, cinnamon, lemon juice and flour.
Roll half the dough into the pie dish and add the apple filling.
Cover with the remaining dough, seal and cut vents.
Bake at 190°C for about 45–55 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Preheat oven to 220°C.
Whisk pumpkin, sugar, eggs, milk, spices and salt until smooth.
Pour into the pie crust.
Bake at 220°C for 15 minutes, then reduce to 175°C and bake for another 35–45 minutes until the center is set.
Cool before slicing.
Prepare and blind-bake the tart shell until lightly golden.
Whisk eggs and sugar, then add lemon juice, zest, cream and melted butter.
Pour the filling into the cooled shell.
Bake at 160°C until the filling is just set with a slight wobble, about 20–25 minutes.
Cool and refrigerate before serving.
Bake and cool the tart shell.
Heat cream until just simmering. Pour over chopped chocolate and let stand for 2 minutes.
Stir until smooth, then mix in butter and sugar if desired.
Pour ganache into the tart shell.
Refrigerate until set, about 2 hours.

ingredients: 2 tbsp apricot jam or strawberry jam
steps: Bake and cool the tart shell.
Spread pastry cream evenly inside the shell.
Arrange sliced or halved strawberries over the cream.
Warm the jam with a little water and brush lightly over the fruit for shine.
Chill until serving.
Whisk egg yolks with sugar until pale, then mix in mascarpone.
Whip egg whites to soft peaks and fold gently into the mascarpone mixture.
Dip ladyfingers briefly in cooled coffee, avoiding over-soaking.
Layer biscuits and mascarpone cream in a dish.
Refrigerate for at least 6 hours and dust with cocoa before serving.
Sprinkle gelatin over cold water and let it bloom.
Warm cream, milk and sugar until the sugar dissolves; do not boil.
Remove from heat, add vanilla and dissolve the gelatin into the warm mixture.
Pour into molds or glasses.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours until set.
Preheat oven to 150°C.
Warm cream with vanilla until hot but not boiling.
Whisk egg yolks with sugar, then gradually whisk in the warm cream.
Pour into ramekins and bake in a water bath for about 35–45 minutes until just set.
Cool and refrigerate. Sprinkle sugar over each top and caramelize with a torch or under a hot grill.
Beat drained ricotta with powdered sugar and vanilla until smooth.
Fold in chocolate chips and pistachios.
Fill cooled cannoli shells with the ricotta mixture just before serving.
Dust with powdered sugar and garnish with pistachios if desired.
Sift almond flour and powdered sugar together.
Whip egg whites with granulated sugar until stiff, glossy peaks form; add coloring if desired.
Fold dry ingredients into the meringue until the batter flows slowly and smoothly.
Pipe small rounds onto a lined tray and rest until a skin forms.
Bake at about 150°C for 12–15 minutes. Cool and sandwich with filling.
Mix flour, yeast, sugar and salt. Add warm milk, egg and butter to form a soft dough.
Knead until smooth, then cover and let rise until doubled.
Roll the dough and cut donut shapes.
Let them rest for 20–30 minutes.
Fry in 175–180°C oil until golden on both sides. Glaze or coat as desired.
Whisk flour, cocoa, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
Add eggs, milk, oil and vanilla and mix just until combined.
Pipe or spoon batter into greased donut molds.
Bake at 175°C for about 10–14 minutes until set.
Cool and dip in chocolate glaze.
Combine flour, yeast, sugar, salt, warm milk, egg and butter into a soft dough.
Knead and let rise until doubled.
Roll into a rectangle and spread with softened butter, brown sugar and cinnamon.
Roll tightly, slice into rounds and place in a greased pan. Let rise again.
Bake at 180°C for about 20–25 minutes. Glaze if desired.
Whisk flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.
Beat eggs with milk, melted butter and vanilla.
Combine wet and dry ingredients without overmixing.
Preheat and lightly grease a waffle iron.
Cook portions of batter until golden and crisp. Serve with fruit or syrup.
Whisk flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.
Mix egg yolks with milk, butter and vanilla, then combine with dry ingredients.
Whip egg whites to soft peaks and fold them gently into the batter.
Cook in a Belgian-style waffle iron until deeply golden and crisp.
Serve warm with fruit, whipped cream or syrup.
Whisk flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.
